text: Weekend again and nobody to call. Spoke to the cashier and that was it for two days.
New city, new job, no friends yet. Ate dinner watching other people's stories on my phone.
Everyone in the group chat is meeting up and nobody asked me. Maybe they forgot. Maybe not.
Since Harold died the evenings are the hardest. His chair, the empty side of the bed.
Surrounded by people at the party and still felt completely alone.
Working from home every day. Some days I realise I haven't spoken out loud since morning.
Miss having someone to tell small things to. The funny thing the bus driver said. Who do I tell?
Kids have all moved away. Big house. Quiet phone.
Long-distance is hard tonight. Bongani's asleep, eight hours ahead. I just want to hear his voice.
Christmas alone this year. Told everyone I'm fine. Watching carols on the TV with a microwave meal.
I'm the only one in my year who doesn't speak the language well. Lunchtimes I sit in the library.
Feeling invisible. Nobody noticed I'd been away for a week.
Messaged four friends to see if anyone wanted to get dinner. Two read it. None replied.
Since the divorce I eat standing up. No point setting the table for one.
Missing my old flatmates. Mia, Juno and the endless 2am kitchen chats.
My husband is right next to me on the sofa and I've never felt more alone.
Lonely Sunday. Walked around the market just to be around people.
Everyone has someone. Couples everywhere at the restaurant. I came by myself and pretended to read.
Ten days in hospital and the only visitor was the chaplain. Kind man. Still.
Abroad for the semester. The others go home at weekends. The halls echo.
I want to be close to someone but every time I try it feels like I'm too much.
Birthday. Facebook messages from people I haven't seen in years. No one to have cake with.
Mamá is so far away. Video calls aren't the same as her hand on my head.
New mum. Everyone asks about the baby. Nobody asks about me.
Called Daniel three times this week. He was always busy. I'm starting to feel like the only one trying.
First night in the empty house after Esi moved out. Even the fridge sounds loud.
Wish I had a friend to go to the cinema with. Went alone. It was fine. Mostly.
I don't fit in here. Not with the parents at the school gate, not at work, not anywhere really.
Night shift on the ward, the patients asleep, the corridors humming. Very alone tonight.
Dad's in the care home now. I visit, but the house feels hollow without him in it.
I keep scrolling through photos of old friends' lives and wondering when I stopped being in them.
Ordered takeaway just to talk to the delivery guy for a minute.
Isolated. The flu means a week indoors and nobody's come by.
My best friend has a new best friend. I can see it in the photos.
Retired last month. Miss the office banter more than I expected. Days are long.
Lonely in a crowded house. Five of us and nobody talks.
The only person who really got me was Nana and she's been gone a year today.
Moved to the countryside for peace and quiet. Got it. Too much of it, maybe.
Watched couples at the beach and felt a pang. Not jealous exactly. Just alone.
Long weekend with no plans. Didn't speak to anyone from Friday night to Monday morning.
I'm the friend people call when they need something. Who do I call?
Saw a group of girls laughing on the train and remembered when that was us. Haven't heard from any of them in ages.
Home from uni for the summer and all my school friends have moved on. Sitting in my old bedroom like a ghost.
Tobi's family is lovely but they speak their language at dinner and I sit there smiling, understanding nothing.
Missing connection. Real connection, not likes.
Walked past our old café and Liv wasn't there, of course. She moved two years ago. Still look every time.
Feeling disconnected from everyone. Like I'm watching life through a window.
Deployed abroad, six months to go. The calls home keep me going but the nights are long.
My son doesn't call much since he moved in with his girlfriend. I don't want to bother him.
No one to share the good news with. Got the promotion and told the cat.
Hard being the only queer person in my town. Hard not having anyone who just gets it.
Ate lunch in my car again. Easier than sitting alone in the canteen.
I miss Callie. Not the relationship, just her. Her company.
Nobody to sit with at the wedding. Spent the reception talking to the bartender.
Sometimes I think if I disappeared for a week no one would notice. Not dramatically. Just honestly.
The new neighbours are nice but they're always busy. Waved hello, that's about it.
Felt lonely at book club tonight even though everyone was friendly. Couldn't find my way into the conversation.
Six weeks since I moved. Still haven't made a single friend here.
Grandma says the worst part of being 90 is that all her friends are gone. I sat with her longer than usual.
Bit lonely. Rain, empty flat, nobody texting back.
Hong Kong was supposed to be an adventure. It's mostly been me, my laptop and the noodle place downstairs.
Eli has his friends, his band, his football. I have Eli. That's not enough and I know it.
Parents' evening alone again. Everyone else came in pairs.
Missing my brother tonight. He used to live round the corner. Now he's an ocean away.
In a new team where everyone's known each other for years. Inside jokes I'm not part of.
Bought two tickets out of habit. Went alone. Left the seat empty next to me.
I'm tired of being the one who reaches out. Stopped this week to see who notices. Nobody so far.
Wandered the museum alone on a Sunday. Beautiful, but I kept turning to say 'look at this' to no one.
Even with Amira here this week I feel lonely. She's here but her mind is somewhere else.
I don't think anyone really knows me. That's the loneliest thought I've had in a while.
